faqs.q: Sec. 2-212. - Disposition of surplus real property.
faqs.a:
(a)
"Real property", as used in this article shall have the meaning as set forth in
section 1-2
of the Arvada City Code, provided nothing in this
section 2-212
shall apply to any real property that is subject to the restrictions or limitations
               on sales or conveyance of park property set forth in chapter 13.2 of the Arvada City
               Charter.
(b)
Upon a determination by the city council that real property owned by the city is no
               longer needed for a city purpose, such real property shall be deemed surplus and may
               be disposed by the city under such terms and conditions as are deemed to be in the
               best interest of the city, giving due consideration to the factors set forth in subsection
               (c) of this
section 2-212
.
(c)
The city shall have discretion in determining the terms and conditions that are in
               the best interest of the city. When making such determination, the city may, but is
               not required, to first consider whether the conveyance of the subject real property
               serves another public purpose performed by a another governmental body, secondly,
               whether the conveyance serves a general social purpose consistent with city goals
               and priorities that is performed by a non-profit agency or entity, or thirdly whether
               the conveyance serves or further a general city goal that is performed by or furthered
               by participation of a private party. Upon a finding of any of the preceding, the city
               may negotiate the terms and conditions of the conveyance of the property to any third
               party.
(d)
In the absence of findings of any of the conditions described in subsection (c) of
               this
section 2-212
, the city shall dispose of surplus real property based on competitive bid or proposal
               following reasonable notice of the offer of sale of the subject surplus real property.
               In considering the proposals or bids submitted from any such solicitation, the city
               shall at all times have discretion in determining what terms or conditions of the
               proposed conveyance are in the best interest of the city. The city may accept or reject
               any bid or proposal or all bids or proposals that the city determines not to be in
               the best interest of the city.
(e)
The city manager, or his/her designee, shall be authorized to sign any contracts or
               related closing documents needed to effect an authorized conveyance pursuant to this
               section. Provided however, in accordance with chapter 13.3 of the City Charter, the
               mayor shall sign any document of conveyance.
(
Ord. No. 4487, § 1, 2-2-2015
)
